Generator functions (yield) simplify iterators. Use: traversing collections, lazy evaluation, streaming data. Built-in: for loops use iterator protocol. Consider performance and maintainability.

Design Patterns.front: How does the Composite pattern work?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Composite.
Design Patterns.normal: Composite: tree structure where individual objects. Component interface with common operations. Leaf and Composite . Use: file system file/directory hierarchy, UI.
Design Patterns.hard: Composite: tree structure where individual objects and compositions are treated uniformly. Component interface with common operations. Leaf (end object) and Composite (container of children). Use: file system (file/directory hierarchy), UI components, organizational charts, AST nodes.
Design Patterns.expert: Composite: tree structure where individual objects and compositions are treated uniformly. Component interface with common operations. Leaf (end object) and Composite (container of children). Use: file system (file/directory hierarchy), UI components, organizational charts, AST nodes. Evaluate trade-offs before deciding.

Design Patterns.front: What is the State pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about State.
Design Patterns.normal: State: allows object to change behavior. Context holds current State object. Each state implements behavior for events. Transitions: state object decides next state. Use: order processing new->paid->shipped, game character.
Design Patterns.hard: State: allows object to change behavior when internal state changes (state machine). Context holds current State object. Each state implements behavior for events. Transitions: state object decides next state. Use: order processing (new->paid->shipped), game character states, workflow engines.
Design Patterns.expert: State: allows object to change behavior when internal state changes (state machine). Context holds current State object. Each state implements behavior for events. Transitions: state object decides next state. Use: order processing (new->paid->shipped), game character states, workflow engines. Evaluate trade-offs before deciding.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Facade pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Facade.
Design Patterns.normal: Facade: provides simplified interface to complex. Reduces coupling, hides complexity. Subsystems don't know facade exists. Use: wrapping complex libraries. Python's __init__.py can serve as facade.
Design Patterns.hard: Facade: provides simplified interface to complex subsystem. Reduces coupling, hides complexity. Subsystems don't know facade exists. Use: wrapping complex libraries (ffmpeg, AWS SDK), simplifying API for common use cases. Python's __init__.py can serve as facade for module package.
Design Patterns.expert: Facade: provides simplified interface to complex subsystem. Reduces coupling, hides complexity. Subsystems don't know facade exists. Use: wrapping complex libraries (ffmpeg, AWS SDK), simplifying API for common use cases. Python's __init__.py can serve as facade for module package. Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Builder pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Builder.
Design Patterns.normal: Builder: separates construction of complex object. Fluent interface (method chaining for readability). Director orchestrates building process (optional). Use: constructing objects with many optional. Python kwargs partially replaces.
Design Patterns.hard: Builder: separates construction of complex object from its representation. Fluent interface (method chaining for readability). Director orchestrates building process (optional). Use: constructing objects with many optional parameters (PizzaBuilder, QueryBuilder, HTML builder). Python kwargs partially replaces.
Design Patterns.expert: Builder: separates construction of complex object from its representation. Fluent interface (method chaining for readability). Director orchestrates building process (optional). Use: constructing objects with many optional parameters (PizzaBuilder, QueryBuilder, HTML builder). Python kwargs partially replaces. Context determines the best approach.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Prototype pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Prototype.
Design Patterns.normal: Prototype: creates new objects by cloning. Python: copy.copy (shallow), copy.deepcopy (deep). Cloning avoids expensive creation. Use: when object creation is expensive. Register prototypes for dynamic configuration.
Design Patterns.hard: Prototype: creates new objects by cloning existing instance. Python: copy.copy (shallow), copy.deepcopy (deep). Cloning avoids expensive creation. Use: when object creation is expensive (DB queries, complex setup), when many similar instances needed. Register prototypes for dynamic configuration.
Design Patterns.expert: Prototype: creates new objects by cloning existing instance. Python: copy.copy (shallow), copy.deepcopy (deep). Cloning avoids expensive creation. Use: when object creation is expensive (DB queries, complex setup), when many similar instances needed. Register prototypes for dynamic configuration. Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: How does the Chain of Responsibility pattern work?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Chain.
Design Patterns.normal: Chain of Responsibility: passes request along. Each handler decides to handle. Python: linked list of handlers. Use: logging severity levels, authentication middleware.
Design Patterns.hard: Chain of Responsibility: passes request along chain of handlers until one handles it. Each handler decides to handle or pass to next. Python: linked list of handlers with handle() method. Use: logging (severity levels), authentication middleware (OAuth, JWT, API key), validation pipelines.
Design Patterns.expert: Chain of Responsibility: passes request along chain of handlers until one handles it. Each handler decides to handle or pass to next. Python: linked list of handlers with handle() method. Use: logging (severity levels), authentication middleware (OAuth, JWT, API key), validation pipelines. Evaluate trade-offs before deciding.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Mediator pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Mediator.
Design Patterns.normal: Mediator: centralizes communication between objects (colleagues). Colleagues don't know each other directly. Reduces coupling, simplifies interactions. Use: chat rooms, GUI dialog. Alternative: publish-subscribe (message broker).
Design Patterns.hard: Mediator: centralizes communication between objects (colleagues). Colleagues don't know each other directly. Reduces coupling, simplifies interactions. Use: chat rooms, GUI dialog (components communicate via dialog), air traffic control. Alternative: publish-subscribe (message broker).
Design Patterns.expert: Mediator: centralizes communication between objects (colleagues). Colleagues don't know each other directly. Reduces coupling, simplifies interactions. Use: chat rooms, GUI dialog (components communicate via dialog), air traffic control. Alternative: publish-subscribe (message broker). Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Memento pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Memento.
Design Patterns.normal: Memento: captures and externalizes object's internal. Originator (creates memento), Caretaker (stores mementos). Use: undo/redo, save points in games. Python: pickle/serialization for state persistence. Memory vs storage trade-off.
Design Patterns.hard: Memento: captures and externalizes object's internal state so it can be restored later. Originator (creates memento), Caretaker (stores mementos). Use: undo/redo, save points in games, checkpoint/rollback. Python: pickle/serialization for state persistence. Memory vs storage trade-off.
Design Patterns.expert: Memento: captures and externalizes object's internal state so it can be restored later. Originator (creates memento), Caretaker (stores mementos). Use: undo/redo, save points in games, checkpoint/rollback. Python: pickle/serialization for state persistence. Memory vs storage trade-off.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Visitor pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Visitor.
Design Patterns.normal: Visitor: separates algorithm from object structure. New operations added without modifying classes. Double dispatch: dynamically dispatches based. Use: AST processing compilers, reporting, validation. Python can use singledispatch.
Design Patterns.hard: Visitor: separates algorithm from object structure. New operations added without modifying classes. Double dispatch: dynamically dispatches based on both visitor's and element's types. Use: AST processing (compilers), reporting, validation over heterogeneous structures. Python can use singledispatch.
Design Patterns.expert: Visitor: separates algorithm from object structure. New operations added without modifying classes. Double dispatch: dynamically dispatches based on both visitor's and element's types. Use: AST processing (compilers), reporting, validation over heterogeneous structures. Python can use singledispatch. Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Interpreter pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Interpreter.
Design Patterns.normal: Interpreter: defines grammar for language, interprets. AST nodes represent grammar rules. Terminal expressions vs non-terminal . Use: DSLs, regex engines, SQL parsers. Python's ast module for Python code.
Design Patterns.hard: Interpreter: defines grammar for language, interprets sentences in that language. AST nodes represent grammar rules. Terminal expressions (literals) vs non-terminal (composite rules). Use: DSLs, regex engines, SQL parsers, configuration language parsers. Python's ast module for Python code parsing.
Design Patterns.expert: Interpreter: defines grammar for language, interprets sentences in that language. AST nodes represent grammar rules. Terminal expressions (literals) vs non-terminal (composite rules). Use: DSLs, regex engines, SQL parsers, configuration language parsers. Python's ast module for Python code parsing. Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: How does the Repository pattern work?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Repository.
Design Patterns.normal: Repository: mediates between domain and data. Provides collection-like interface for accessing domain. Decouples business logic from data access. Use: complex queries, testability mock repository. Python: SQLAlchemy session can serve.
Design Patterns.hard: Repository: mediates between domain and data mapping layers. Provides collection-like interface for accessing domain objects. Decouples business logic from data access. Use: complex queries, testability (mock repository), multiple data sources. Python: SQLAlchemy session can serve as repository pattern.
Design Patterns.expert: Repository: mediates between domain and data mapping layers. Provides collection-like interface for accessing domain objects. Decouples business logic from data access. Use: complex queries, testability (mock repository), multiple data sources. Python: SQLAlchemy session can serve as repository pattern. Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Data Mapper pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Data.
Design Patterns.normal: Data Mapper: separates in-memory objects. Maps between object properties and DB. Rows -> objects, objects -> rows. No persistence logic in domain objects. SQLAlchemy ORM implements data mapper. Active Record Django ORM combines domain.
Design Patterns.hard: Data Mapper: separates in-memory objects from database. Maps between object properties and DB columns. Rows -> objects, objects -> rows. No persistence logic in domain objects. SQLAlchemy ORM implements data mapper. Active Record (Django ORM) combines domain and persistence logic.
Design Patterns.expert: Data Mapper: separates in-memory objects from database. Maps between object properties and DB columns. Rows -> objects, objects -> rows. No persistence logic in domain objects. SQLAlchemy ORM implements data mapper. Active Record (Django ORM) combines domain and persistence logic. Context determines the best approach.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Dependency Injection pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Dependency.
Design Patterns.normal: DI: passes dependencies into object . Inversion of Control: framework manages dependencies. Benefits: loose coupling, testability , flexibility. Python: simple argument injection, or frameworks. Without DI: hard-coded dependencies.
Design Patterns.hard: DI: passes dependencies into object (constructor, setter, or interface injection). Inversion of Control: framework manages dependencies. Benefits: loose coupling, testability (mock dependencies), flexibility. Python: simple argument injection, or frameworks (FastAPI Depends). Without DI: hard-coded dependencies.
Design Patterns.expert: DI: passes dependencies into object (constructor, setter, or interface injection). Inversion of Control: framework manages dependencies. Benefits: loose coupling, testability (mock dependencies), flexibility. Python: simple argument injection, or frameworks (FastAPI Depends). Without DI: hard-coded dependencies. Evaluate trade-offs before deciding.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Inversion of Control (IoC) principle?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Inversion.
Design Patterns.normal: IoC: framework calls into application code. Hollywood principle: don't call us, we'll. DI is form of IoC. Event-driven programming, template method, service locator. Spring, FastAPI, Django use IoC.
Design Patterns.hard: IoC: framework calls into application code (instead of application calling library). Hollywood principle: don't call us, we'll call you. DI is form of IoC. Event-driven programming, template method, service locator all IoC. Spring, FastAPI, Django use IoC for component wiring.
Design Patterns.expert: IoC: framework calls into application code (instead of application calling library). Hollywood principle: don't call us, we'll call you. DI is form of IoC. Event-driven programming, template method, service locator all IoC. Spring, FastAPI, Django use IoC for component wiring. Context determines the best approach.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the ActiveRecord pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about ActiveRecord.
Design Patterns.normal: ActiveRecord: domain object is also responsible. Each DB row is object. Methods: save, update, delete, find. Django ORM, Ruby on Rails ActiveRecord. Simple but violates single-responsibility. Less coupling: Data Mapper separates concerns.
Design Patterns.hard: ActiveRecord: domain object is also responsible for persistence. Each DB row is object. Methods: save, update, delete, find. Django ORM, Ruby on Rails ActiveRecord. Simple but violates single-responsibility. Less coupling: Data Mapper (SQLAlchemy) separates concerns.
Design Patterns.expert: ActiveRecord: domain object is also responsible for persistence. Each DB row is object. Methods: save, update, delete, find. Django ORM, Ruby on Rails ActiveRecord. Simple but violates single-responsibility. Less coupling: Data Mapper (SQLAlchemy) separates concerns. Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: How does the Object Pool pattern work?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Object.
Design Patterns.normal: Object Pool: reusable pool of objects. Thread safety: acquire/release with locking. Use: database connections psycopg2 pool, thread. Pre-allocation vs lazy allocation. LRU cleanup of idle objects.
Design Patterns.hard: Object Pool: reusable pool of objects (expensive to create/recycle). Borrow-return lifecycle. Thread safety: acquire/release with locking. Use: database connections (psycopg2 pool), thread pools (concurrent.futures), network connections. Pre-allocation vs lazy allocation. LRU cleanup of idle objects.
Design Patterns.expert: Object Pool: reusable pool of objects (expensive to create/recycle). Borrow-return lifecycle. Thread safety: acquire/release with locking. Use: database connections (psycopg2 pool), thread pools (concurrent.futures), network connections. Pre-allocation vs lazy allocation. LRU cleanup of idle objects. Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Lazy Loading pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Lazy.
Design Patterns.normal: Lazy loading: defer object initialization until. Types: lazy initialization. Use: expensive resources , large collections. Python: @property lazy loading, descriptor protocol.
Design Patterns.hard: Lazy loading: defer object initialization until needed. Types: lazy initialization (create on first access), virtual proxy (stand-in object), value holder (wrapper), ghost (partially loaded object). Use: expensive resources (DB queries, file reads), large collections. Python: @property lazy loading, descriptor protocol.
Design Patterns.expert: Lazy loading: defer object initialization until needed. Types: lazy initialization (create on first access), virtual proxy (stand-in object), value holder (wrapper), ghost (partially loaded object). Use: expensive resources (DB queries, file reads), large collections. Python: @property lazy loading, descriptor protocol. Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Service Locator pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Service.
Design Patterns.normal: Service Locator: central registry for services. Components request services from locator. Anti-pattern critique: hides dependencies, makes testing. Use: legacy systems, dynamic service resolution. Python: module-level dictionary of services.
Design Patterns.hard: Service Locator: central registry for services. Components request services from locator. Anti-pattern critique: hides dependencies, makes testing harder (global mutable reference). DI preferred. Use: legacy systems, dynamic service resolution, plugin architectures. Python: module-level dictionary of services.
Design Patterns.expert: Service Locator: central registry for services. Components request services from locator. Anti-pattern critique: hides dependencies, makes testing harder (global mutable reference). DI preferred. Use: legacy systems, dynamic service resolution, plugin architectures. Python: module-level dictionary of services. Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Data Transfer Object (DTO) pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Data.
Design Patterns.normal: DTO: simple object carrying data between. No business logic. Serialized/deserialized (JSON, Protobuf, Avro). Python: dataclass, NamedTuple, Pydantic model. Use: API request/response, between microservices, avoid.
Design Patterns.hard: DTO: simple object carrying data between processes (network, service boundaries). No business logic. Serialized/deserialized (JSON, Protobuf, Avro). Python: dataclass, NamedTuple, Pydantic model. Use: API request/response, between microservices, avoid exposing internal entities.
Design Patterns.expert: DTO: simple object carrying data between processes (network, service boundaries). No business logic. Serialized/deserialized (JSON, Protobuf, Avro). Python: dataclass, NamedTuple, Pydantic model. Use: API request/response, between microservices, avoid exposing internal entities. Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the DAO (Data Access Object) pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Data.
Design Patterns.normal: DAO: abstracts persistence operations behind interface. Separate from business logic. Implementation per data source . Repository vs DAO: repository is domain-focused. Python: DAO generic with SQLAlchemy session. Test: mock DAO interface.
Design Patterns.hard: DAO: abstracts persistence operations (CRUD) behind interface. Separate from business logic. Implementation per data source (SQL, NoSQL, file). Repository vs DAO: repository is domain-focused, DAO is data-focused. Python: DAO generic with SQLAlchemy session. Test: mock DAO interface.
Design Patterns.expert: DAO: abstracts persistence operations (CRUD) behind interface. Separate from business logic. Implementation per data source (SQL, NoSQL, file). Repository vs DAO: repository is domain-focused, DAO is data-focused. Python: DAO generic with SQLAlchemy session. Test: mock DAO interface. Context determines the best approach.

Design Patterns.front: How does the Concrete Factory vs Abstract Factory differ?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Concrete.
Design Patterns.normal: Simple Factory: single class returns product. Factory Method: inheritance-based, subclass creates product. Abstract Factory: interface for creating related. Abstract Factory extends Factory Method.
Design Patterns.hard: Simple Factory: single class (static method) returns product. Factory Method: inheritance-based, subclass creates product. Abstract Factory: interface for creating related families, implemented by concrete factories (Windows/Mac/Linux UI factories). Abstract Factory extends Factory Method with multiple products.
Design Patterns.expert: Simple Factory: single class (static method) returns product. Factory Method: inheritance-based, subclass creates product. Abstract Factory: interface for creating related families, implemented by concrete factories (Windows/Mac/Linux UI factories). Abstract Factory extends Factory Method with multiple products. Context determines the best approach.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Bridge pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Bridge.
Design Patterns.normal: Bridge: decouples abstraction from implementation. Uses composition instead of inheritance . Abstraction delegates to Implementor. Use: cross-platform graphics Windows/DirectX vs Linux/Vulkan. Prevents class explosion (platform * feature).
Design Patterns.hard: Bridge: decouples abstraction from implementation so both vary independently. Uses composition (has-a) instead of inheritance (is-a). Abstraction delegates to Implementor. Use: cross-platform graphics (Windows/DirectX vs Linux/Vulkan), device drivers, UI frameworks. Prevents class explosion (platform * feature).
Design Patterns.expert: Bridge: decouples abstraction from implementation so both vary independently. Uses composition (has-a) instead of inheritance (is-a). Abstraction delegates to Implementor. Use: cross-platform graphics (Windows/DirectX vs Linux/Vulkan), device drivers, UI frameworks. Prevents class explosion (platform * feature). Consider performance and maintainability.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Flyweight pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Flyweight.
Design Patterns.normal: Flyweight: shares object state to minimize. Intrinsic vs extrinsic . Factory manages flyweight pool. Use: character rendering shared glyph data. Python: interning of small strings is.
Design Patterns.hard: Flyweight: shares object state to minimize memory. Intrinsic (shared, immutable) vs extrinsic (context, passed in). Factory manages flyweight pool. Use: character rendering (shared glyph data), game particles (shared texture), thread-safe connections. Python: interning of small strings is flyweight pattern.
Design Patterns.expert: Flyweight: shares object state to minimize memory. Intrinsic (shared, immutable) vs extrinsic (context, passed in). Factory manages flyweight pool. Use: character rendering (shared glyph data), game particles (shared texture), thread-safe connections. Python: interning of small strings is flyweight pattern. Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Null Object pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Null.
Design Patterns.normal: Null Object: replaces None/null checks No-op. Use: optional dependencies, default behaviors, eliminate. Python: object with __bool__ = False. Example: empty collection vs null.
Design Patterns.hard: Null Object: replaces None/null checks with do-nothing object implementing same interface. No-op methods. Use: optional dependencies, default behaviors, eliminate conditionals. Python: object with __bool__ = False. Example: empty collection vs null in streaming data processing.
Design Patterns.expert: Null Object: replaces None/null checks with do-nothing object implementing same interface. No-op methods. Use: optional dependencies, default behaviors, eliminate conditionals. Python: object with __bool__ = False. Example: empty collection vs null in streaming data processing. Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the MVC (Model-View-Controller) pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Model.
Design Patterns.normal: Model: business logic + data View. Controller: handles input, updates model, selects. Django: Model-View-Template (MTV) variant. FastAPI + Jinja2: MVT. Separation of concerns: test model independently. Modern SPA: API + frontend .
Design Patterns.hard: Model: business logic + data. View: presentation/UI. Controller: handles input, updates model, selects view. Django: Model-View-Template (MTV) variant. FastAPI + Jinja2: MVT. Separation of concerns: test model independently, swap views. Modern SPA: API (model) + frontend (view).
Design Patterns.expert: Model: business logic + data. View: presentation/UI. Controller: handles input, updates model, selects view. Django: Model-View-Template (MTV) variant. FastAPI + Jinja2: MVT. Separation of concerns: test model independently, swap views. Modern SPA: API (model) + frontend (view). Consider performance and maintainability.

Design Patterns.front: How does the MVVM (Model-View-ViewModel) pattern work?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about MVVM.
Design Patterns.normal: MVVM: ViewModel exposes model data. Two-way data binding: View changes automatically. WPF, Angular, Vue, Knockout. ViewModel is state + commands. Test ViewModel independently of View .
Design Patterns.hard: MVVM: ViewModel exposes model data as observable properties for View binding. Two-way data binding: View changes automatically update ViewModel and vice versa. WPF, Angular, Vue, Knockout. ViewModel is state + commands for view. Test ViewModel independently of View (no UI dependency).
Design Patterns.expert: MVVM: ViewModel exposes model data as observable properties for View binding. Two-way data binding: View changes automatically update ViewModel and vice versa. WPF, Angular, Vue, Knockout. ViewModel is state + commands for view. Test ViewModel independently of View (no UI dependency). Context determines the best approach.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Difference between MVC and MVVM?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Difference.
Design Patterns.normal: MVC: Controller handles user input, updates. MVVM: ViewModel exposes data + commands. MVVM has automatic two-way binding . MVC more common for server-side.
Design Patterns.hard: MVC: Controller handles user input, updates Model, selects View. MVVM: ViewModel exposes data + commands via observable properties, View binds to them. MVVM has automatic two-way binding (less glue code). MVC more common for server-side (Django, Rails), MVVM for client-side (Angular, WPF).
Design Patterns.expert: MVC: Controller handles user input, updates Model, selects View. MVVM: ViewModel exposes data + commands via observable properties, View binds to them. MVVM has automatic two-way binding (less glue code). MVC more common for server-side (Django, Rails), MVVM for client-side (Angular, WPF). Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Event Sourcing pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Event.
Design Patterns.normal: Event Sourcing: state represented as sequence. Current state = fold/reduce of events. Benefits: audit trail, temporal queries, rebuild. Stores: EventStoreDB, Kafka. Challenges: schema evolution, event versioning, eventual.
Design Patterns.hard: Event Sourcing: state represented as sequence of events. Current state = fold/reduce of events. Benefits: audit trail, temporal queries, rebuild state from scratch, event-driven architecture. Stores: EventStoreDB, Kafka. Challenges: schema evolution, event versioning, eventual consistency.
Design Patterns.expert: Event Sourcing: state represented as sequence of events. Current state = fold/reduce of events. Benefits: audit trail, temporal queries, rebuild state from scratch, event-driven architecture. Stores: EventStoreDB, Kafka. Challenges: schema evolution, event versioning, eventual consistency. Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: What is the CQRS pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about CQRS.
Design Patterns.normal: CQRS: separate read and write models. Command: mutates state (write). Query: retrieves state (read). Separate databases optimized per operation. Benefits: independent scaling, optimized read models. Simple CQRS: separate service interfaces. Full CQRS + Event Sourcing.
Design Patterns.hard: CQRS: separate read and write models. Command: mutates state (write). Query: retrieves state (read). Separate databases optimized per operation. Benefits: independent scaling, optimized read models (denormalized), write model enforces domain rules. Simple CQRS: separate service interfaces. Full CQRS + Event Sourcing.
Design Patterns.expert: CQRS: separate read and write models. Command: mutates state (write). Query: retrieves state (read). Separate databases optimized per operation. Benefits: independent scaling, optimized read models (denormalized), write model enforces domain rules. Simple CQRS: separate service interfaces. Full CQRS + Event Sourcing. Consider performance and maintainability.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Saga orchestration pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Saga.
Design Patterns.normal: Saga: distributed transaction across microservices. Choreography: each service produces events triggering. Orchestration: central coordinator orchestrator tells services. Compensating actions (undo) on failure. Use: order processing .
Design Patterns.hard: Saga: distributed transaction across microservices. Choreography: each service produces events triggering next service. Orchestration: central coordinator (orchestrator) tells services what to do. Compensating actions (undo) on failure. Use: order processing (create order -> reserve inventory -> charge payment -> ship order).
Design Patterns.expert: Saga: distributed transaction across microservices. Choreography: each service produces events triggering next service. Orchestration: central coordinator (orchestrator) tells services what to do. Compensating actions (undo) on failure. Use: order processing (create order -> reserve inventory -> charge payment -> ship order). Context determines the best approach.

Design Patterns.front: How does the Outbox pattern work?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Outbox.
Design Patterns.normal: Outbox: transactional outbox table for reliable. In same DB transaction as business. Outbox reader/relay publishes events to message. Guarantees: exactly-once delivery (no dual-write problem). Cancel outbox vs domain outbox.
Design Patterns.hard: Outbox: transactional outbox table for reliable event publishing. In same DB transaction as business operation. Outbox reader/relay publishes events to message broker (CDC change data capture - Debezium, or polling). Guarantees: exactly-once delivery (no dual-write problem). Cancel outbox vs domain outbox.
Design Patterns.expert: Outbox: transactional outbox table for reliable event publishing. In same DB transaction as business operation. Outbox reader/relay publishes events to message broker (CDC change data capture - Debezium, or polling). Guarantees: exactly-once delivery (no dual-write problem). Cancel outbox vs domain outbox. Context determines the best approach.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Saga choreography pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Saga.
Design Patterns.normal: Saga choreography: no central coordinator. Each service after action publishes event. Compensating events on failure. Pros: decentralized, simpler. Cons: hard to track, cyclic dependencies. Use: simpler workflows. Async communication via message broker .
Design Patterns.hard: Saga choreography: no central coordinator. Each service after action publishes event, next service listens and acts. Compensating events on failure. Pros: decentralized, simpler. Cons: hard to track, cyclic dependencies. Use: simpler workflows. Async communication via message broker (RabbitMQ, Kafka).
Design Patterns.expert: Saga choreography: no central coordinator. Each service after action publishes event, next service listens and acts. Compensating events on failure. Pros: decentralized, simpler. Cons: hard to track, cyclic dependencies. Use: simpler workflows. Async communication via message broker (RabbitMQ, Kafka). Consider performance and maintainability.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Circuit Breaker pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Circuit.
Design Patterns.normal: Circuit Breaker: prevents cascading failures. States: closed normal, calls pass, open. Metrics: failure count/threshold, timeout. Recovery: after reset timeout, allow test. Tools: Hystrix, resilience4j, Python pybreaker.
Design Patterns.hard: Circuit Breaker: prevents cascading failures by stopping calls to failing service. States: closed (normal, calls pass), open (failing, calls fail fast), half-open (test calls after timeout). Metrics: failure count/threshold, timeout. Recovery: after reset timeout, allow test calls. Tools: Hystrix, resilience4j, Python pybreaker.
Design Patterns.expert: Circuit Breaker: prevents cascading failures by stopping calls to failing service. States: closed (normal, calls pass), open (failing, calls fail fast), half-open (test calls after timeout). Metrics: failure count/threshold, timeout. Recovery: after reset timeout, allow test calls. Tools: Hystrix, resilience4j, Python pybreaker. Context determines the best approach.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Bulkhead pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Bulkhead.
Design Patterns.normal: Bulkhead: isolates resources into pools. Thread pools per service, connection pools. Fixed number of connections/threads per partition. Compartmentalization: ship hull analogy. Use: separate thread pools for different.
Design Patterns.hard: Bulkhead: isolates resources into pools so failure in one pool doesn't cascade. Thread pools per service, connection pools per downstream. Fixed number of connections/threads per partition. Compartmentalization: ship hull analogy. Use: separate thread pools for different API endpoints, separate connection pools per DB.
Design Patterns.expert: Bulkhead: isolates resources into pools so failure in one pool doesn't cascade. Thread pools per service, connection pools per downstream. Fixed number of connections/threads per partition. Compartmentalization: ship hull analogy. Use: separate thread pools for different API endpoints, separate connection pools per DB. Context determines the best approach.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Retry pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Retry.
Design Patterns.normal: Retry: automatically retry failed operations . Wait strategies: fixed, incremental, exponential backoff. Max retries + timeout Idempotency required. Use: network calls, DB operations, distributed. Exponential backoff with jitter prevents thundering.
Design Patterns.hard: Retry: automatically retry failed operations (transient faults). Wait strategies: fixed, incremental, exponential backoff, jitter. Max retries + timeout. Idempotency required. Use: network calls, DB operations, distributed systems. Exponential backoff with jitter prevents thundering herd.
Design Patterns.expert: Retry: automatically retry failed operations (transient faults). Wait strategies: fixed, incremental, exponential backoff, jitter. Max retries + timeout. Idempotency required. Use: network calls, DB operations, distributed systems. Exponential backoff with jitter prevents thundering herd. Context determines the best approach.

Design Patterns.front: How does the Throttling pattern work?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Throttling.
Design Patterns.normal: Throttling: rate limit requests to protect. Strategies: token bucket, leaky bucket, sliding. Levels: per-user, per-IP, per-endpoint. Response: 429 Too Many Requests. Queuing: buffer requests instead of rejecting.
Design Patterns.hard: Throttling: rate limit requests to protect system. Strategies: token bucket, leaky bucket, sliding window, fixed window. Levels: per-user, per-IP, per-endpoint. Response: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After header. Queuing: buffer requests instead of rejecting.
Design Patterns.expert: Throttling: rate limit requests to protect system. Strategies: token bucket, leaky bucket, sliding window, fixed window. Levels: per-user, per-IP, per-endpoint. Response: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After header. Queuing: buffer requests instead of rejecting. Evaluate trade-offs before deciding.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Strangler Fig pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Strangler.
Design Patterns.normal: Strangler Fig: gradually replace legacy system. Intercept calls to legacy, route. Eventually legacy system strangled. Use: monolith to microservices migration. Proxy/gateway routes by URL path/user ID. Modernize piece by piece, production proven.
Design Patterns.hard: Strangler Fig: gradually replace legacy system with new system. Intercept calls to legacy, route to new functionality incrementally. Eventually legacy system strangled. Use: monolith to microservices migration. Proxy/gateway routes by URL path/user ID. Modernize piece by piece, production proven.
Design Patterns.expert: Strangler Fig: gradually replace legacy system with new system. Intercept calls to legacy, route to new functionality incrementally. Eventually legacy system strangled. Use: monolith to microservices migration. Proxy/gateway routes by URL path/user ID. Modernize piece by piece, production proven. Context determines the best approach.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Sidecar pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Sidecar.
Design Patterns.normal: Sidecar: deploy helper component alongside main. Shared lifecycle, network, storage. Use: logging, monitoring, proxy, sync, TLS. Service mesh uses sidecar proxies (Envoy). Vault agent sidecar for secret rotation. Offload concerns from main application container.
Design Patterns.hard: Sidecar: deploy helper component alongside main application (same pod). Shared lifecycle, network, storage. Use: logging, monitoring, proxy, sync, TLS termination. Service mesh uses sidecar proxies (Envoy). Vault agent sidecar for secret rotation. Offload concerns from main application container.
Design Patterns.expert: Sidecar: deploy helper component alongside main application (same pod). Shared lifecycle, network, storage. Use: logging, monitoring, proxy, sync, TLS termination. Service mesh uses sidecar proxies (Envoy). Vault agent sidecar for secret rotation. Offload concerns from main application container. Evaluate trade-offs before deciding.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Ambassador pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Ambassador.
Design Patterns.normal: Ambassador: proxy service sitting in front. Handles cross-cutting concerns: authentication, rate limiting. Sidecar vs Ambassador: Ambassador acts. K8s: ambassador pattern as API Gateway.
Design Patterns.hard: Ambassador: proxy service sitting in front of main service. Handles cross-cutting concerns: authentication, rate limiting, caching, circuit breaking, retries. Sidecar vs Ambassador: Ambassador acts as intermediary, often outside application process. K8s: ambassador pattern as API Gateway.
Design Patterns.expert: Ambassador: proxy service sitting in front of main service. Handles cross-cutting concerns: authentication, rate limiting, caching, circuit breaking, retries. Sidecar vs Ambassador: Ambassador acts as intermediary, often outside application process. K8s: ambassador pattern as API Gateway. Evaluate trade-offs before deciding.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Adapter (microservices) pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Adapter.
Design Patterns.normal: Adapter: translates between incompatible service interfaces. Protocol conversion SOAP to REST, data. Use: integrating legacy services, API versioning. Implemented as separate microservice .
Design Patterns.hard: Adapter: translates between incompatible service interfaces. Protocol conversion (SOAP to REST), data format transformation (XML to JSON), version translation. Use: integrating legacy services, API versioning, vendor-specific adapters. Implemented as separate microservice (API gateway adapter).
Design Patterns.expert: Adapter: translates between incompatible service interfaces. Protocol conversion (SOAP to REST), data format transformation (XML to JSON), version translation. Use: integrating legacy services, API versioning, vendor-specific adapters. Implemented as separate microservice (API gateway adapter). Consider performance and maintainability.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Backends for Frontends (BFF) pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Backends.
Design Patterns.normal: BFF: separate backend per client type. Each BFF optimized for specific client. Avoids generic API that serves all. Co-located with client team. Simplifies frontend, backend tailored to use.
Design Patterns.hard: BFF: separate backend per client type (mobile, web, desktop). Each BFF optimized for specific client needs (payload size, data format, API design). Avoids generic API that serves all clients poorly. Co-located with client team. Simplifies frontend, backend tailored to use case.
Design Patterns.expert: BFF: separate backend per client type (mobile, web, desktop). Each BFF optimized for specific client needs (payload size, data format, API design). Avoids generic API that serves all clients poorly. Co-located with client team. Simplifies frontend, backend tailored to use case. Evaluate trade-offs before deciding.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the API Gateway pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Gateway.
Design Patterns.normal: API Gateway: single entry point. Routing, authentication, rate limiting, caching, request/response. Cross-cutting concerns handled centrally. Tools: Kong, NGINX Plus, AWS API. Backend for Frontends is variation .
Design Patterns.hard: API Gateway: single entry point for multiple microservices. Routing, authentication, rate limiting, caching, request/response transformation, aggregation. Cross-cutting concerns handled centrally. Tools: Kong, NGINX Plus, AWS API Gateway, Zuul. Backend for Frontends is variation (per-client gateway).
Design Patterns.expert: API Gateway: single entry point for multiple microservices. Routing, authentication, rate limiting, caching, request/response transformation, aggregation. Cross-cutting concerns handled centrally. Tools: Kong, NGINX Plus, AWS API Gateway, Zuul. Backend for Frontends is variation (per-client gateway). Consider performance and maintainability.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Gateway Aggregation pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Gateway.
Design Patterns.normal: API Gateway aggregates responses from multiple. Request -> gateway -> parallel calls. Reduces client round trips. Use: dashboard that needs data. Risk: gateway becomes bottleneck. Use async I/O for parallel calls.
Design Patterns.hard: API Gateway aggregates responses from multiple services into single response. Request -> gateway -> parallel calls to services -> combined response. Reduces client round trips. Use: dashboard that needs data from multiple services. Risk: gateway becomes bottleneck. Use async I/O for parallel calls.
Design Patterns.expert: API Gateway aggregates responses from multiple services into single response. Request -> gateway -> parallel calls to services -> combined response. Reduces client round trips. Use: dashboard that needs data from multiple services. Risk: gateway becomes bottleneck. Use async I/O for parallel calls. Consider performance and maintainability.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Gateway Routing pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Gateway.
Design Patterns.normal: Route requests to appropriate service based. Example: /users/* -> user-service, /orders/* ->. Load balancing across service instances. Path-based routing in ingress controllers. Content-based routing (request type/header). Blue-green via routing rules.
Design Patterns.hard: Route requests to appropriate service based on path, header, or query parameter. Example: /users/* -> user-service, /orders/* -> order-service. Load balancing across service instances. Path-based routing in ingress controllers. Content-based routing (request type/header). Blue-green via routing rules.
Design Patterns.expert: Route requests to appropriate service based on path, header, or query parameter. Example: /users/* -> user-service, /orders/* -> order-service. Load balancing across service instances. Path-based routing in ingress controllers. Content-based routing (request type/header). Blue-green via routing rules. Consider performance and maintainability.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Choreography pattern in microservices?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Choreography.
Design Patterns.normal: Choreography: each service makes local decisions. Other services react to events. No central coordinator. Used in event-driven architecture Decentralized. Events published to message broker . Event-driven sagas use choreography.
Design Patterns.hard: Choreography: each service makes local decisions and publishes events. Other services react to events. No central coordinator. Used in event-driven architecture. Decentralized, but complex to trace and debug. Events published to message broker (Kafka, RabbitMQ). Event-driven sagas use choreography.
Design Patterns.expert: Choreography: each service makes local decisions and publishes events. Other services react to events. No central coordinator. Used in event-driven architecture. Decentralized, but complex to trace and debug. Events published to message broker (Kafka, RabbitMQ). Event-driven sagas use choreography. Consider performance and maintainability.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Orchestration pattern in microservices.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Orchestration.
Design Patterns.normal: Orchestration: central orchestrator service coordinates workflow. Calls services in sequence/parallel, handles failures. More control, easier monitoring (state machine). Risk: orchestrator becomes monolith. Workflow engines: Temporal, Camunda, AWS Step.
Design Patterns.hard: Orchestration: central orchestrator service coordinates workflow. Calls services in sequence/parallel, handles failures, compensates. More control, easier monitoring (state machine). Risk: orchestrator becomes monolith. Workflow engines: Temporal, Camunda, AWS Step Functions. Orchestration-based sagas.
Design Patterns.expert: Orchestration: central orchestrator service coordinates workflow. Calls services in sequence/parallel, handles failures, compensates. More control, easier monitoring (state machine). Risk: orchestrator becomes monolith. Workflow engines: Temporal, Camunda, AWS Step Functions. Orchestration-based sagas. Consider performance and maintainability.

Design Patterns.front: How does the Domain Event pattern work?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Domain.
Design Patterns.normal: Domain Event: significant business event captured. Raised when something notable happens . Event handlers trigger side effects . DDD tactical pattern. Stored in event store for audit.
Design Patterns.hard: Domain Event: significant business event captured as first-class object. Raised when something notable happens (OrderPlaced, InvoicePaid). Event handlers trigger side effects (send email, update inventory, publish integration event). DDD tactical pattern. Stored in event store for audit trail.
Design Patterns.expert: Domain Event: significant business event captured as first-class object. Raised when something notable happens (OrderPlaced, InvoicePaid). Event handlers trigger side effects (send email, update inventory, publish integration event). DDD tactical pattern. Stored in event store for audit trail. Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Value Object pattern (DDD).
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Value.
Design Patterns.normal: Value Object: immutable object defined. Equality by value. Examples: Money amount + currency, Address. No ID field Automatically interchangeable. Python: dataclass(frozen=True), NamedTuple. Persistence: embedded vs separate table.
Design Patterns.hard: Value Object: immutable object defined by attributes (not identity). Equality by value. Examples: Money (amount + currency), Address (street + city + zip), Color (RGB). No ID field. Automatically interchangeable. Python: dataclass(frozen=True), NamedTuple. Persistence: embedded (MongoDB document) vs separate table.
Design Patterns.expert: Value Object: immutable object defined by attributes (not identity). Equality by value. Examples: Money (amount + currency), Address (street + city + zip), Color (RGB). No ID field. Automatically interchangeable. Python: dataclass(frozen=True), NamedTuple. Persistence: embedded (MongoDB document) vs separate table. Consider performance and maintainability.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Entity pattern (DDD)?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Entity.
Design Patterns.normal: Entity: object with distinct identity ID. Equality by identity Mutable. Examples: User user_id, Order order_id, Product. Repository pattern stores entities. DDD aggregate: cluster of entities.
Design Patterns.hard: Entity: object with distinct identity (ID) that persists across changes. Equality by identity. Mutable. Examples: User (user_id), Order (order_id), Product (product_id). Repository pattern stores entities. DDD aggregate: cluster of entities with root entity guarding invariants.
Design Patterns.expert: Entity: object with distinct identity (ID) that persists across changes. Equality by identity. Mutable. Examples: User (user_id), Order (order_id), Product (product_id). Repository pattern stores entities. DDD aggregate: cluster of entities with root entity guarding invariants. Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Aggregate pattern (DDD).
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Aggregate.
Design Patterns.normal: Aggregate: cluster of domain objects treated. Aggregate Root: single entry point entity. Clients modify aggregate only through root. Invariants enforced by root. Transactional boundary: entire aggregate loaded/saved atomically. Example: Order aggregate . Keep aggregates small.
Design Patterns.hard: Aggregate: cluster of domain objects treated as unit. Aggregate Root: single entry point entity. Clients modify aggregate only through root. Invariants enforced by root. Transactional boundary: entire aggregate loaded/saved atomically. Example: Order aggregate (Order as root with OrderLines). Keep aggregates small.
Design Patterns.expert: Aggregate: cluster of domain objects treated as unit. Aggregate Root: single entry point entity. Clients modify aggregate only through root. Invariants enforced by root. Transactional boundary: entire aggregate loaded/saved atomically. Example: Order aggregate (Order as root with OrderLines). Keep aggregates small. Consider performance and maintainability.

Design Patterns.front: How does the Repository pattern differ in DDD vs generic?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Repository.
Design Patterns.normal: DDD Repository: collection of aggregates, domain-focused. Generic Repository: CRUD operations on any. DDD Repository is per aggregate root. Avoid generic repository (leaky abstraction). Repository + Unit of Work.
Design Patterns.hard: DDD Repository: collection of aggregates, domain-focused queries, returns domain objects. Generic Repository: CRUD operations on any entity. DDD Repository is per aggregate root, uses Ubiquitous Language. Avoid generic repository (leaky abstraction). Repository + Unit of Work for transaction management.
Design Patterns.expert: DDD Repository: collection of aggregates, domain-focused queries, returns domain objects. Generic Repository: CRUD operations on any entity. DDD Repository is per aggregate root, uses Ubiquitous Language. Avoid generic repository (leaky abstraction). Repository + Unit of Work for transaction management. Context determines the best approach.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Unit of Work pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Unit.
Design Patterns.normal: Unit of Work: tracks changes. Commits all changes as single transaction. Ensures: all saves succeed or all. SQLAlchemy Session is Unit of Work. Closely tied to Repository pattern. New session per request/use case.
Design Patterns.hard: Unit of Work: tracks changes to objects during business transaction. Commits all changes as single transaction. Ensures: all saves succeed or all rollback. SQLAlchemy Session is Unit of Work. Django Transaction.atomic. Closely tied to Repository pattern. New session per request/use case.
Design Patterns.expert: Unit of Work: tracks changes to objects during business transaction. Commits all changes as single transaction. Ensures: all saves succeed or all rollback. SQLAlchemy Session is Unit of Work. Django Transaction.atomic. Closely tied to Repository pattern. New session per request/use case. Consider performance and maintainability.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Specification pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Specification.
Design Patterns.normal: Specification: business rule expressed as predicate. Combines using AND/OR/NOT Reusable, composable. Use: query building, validation, business rule. Python: callable classes with __and__, __or__. SQLAlchemy hybrid: criteria + Python check. ORM integration: filter by specification.
Design Patterns.hard: Specification: business rule expressed as predicate object. Combines using AND/OR/NOT. Reusable, composable. Use: query building, validation, business rule checking. Python: callable classes with __and__, __or__. SQLAlchemy hybrid: criteria + Python check. ORM integration: filter by specification.
Design Patterns.expert: Specification: business rule expressed as predicate object. Combines using AND/OR/NOT. Reusable, composable. Use: query building, validation, business rule checking. Python: callable classes with __and__, __or__. SQLAlchemy hybrid: criteria + Python check. ORM integration: filter by specification. Consider performance and maintainability.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Layer Supertype pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Layer.
Design Patterns.normal: Layer Supertype: base class for all. Provides common behavior: ID generation, timestamp. Python: BaseModel (Pydantic), mixins (TimestampMixin, IDMixin). Reduces code duplication, enforces conventions. Used in all layers .
Design Patterns.hard: Layer Supertype: base class for all objects in layer. Provides common behavior: ID generation, timestamp management, serialization, equality operators. Python: BaseModel (Pydantic), mixins (TimestampMixin, IDMixin). Reduces code duplication, enforces conventions. Used in all layers (domain, persistence, presentation).
Design Patterns.expert: Layer Supertype: base class for all objects in layer. Provides common behavior: ID generation, timestamp management, serialization, equality operators. Python: BaseModel (Pydantic), mixins (TimestampMixin, IDMixin). Reduces code duplication, enforces conventions. Used in all layers (domain, persistence, presentation). Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Separated Interface pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Separated.
Design Patterns.normal: Separated Interface: define interface in separate. Decouples client from implementation. Allows multiple implementations swapped at runtime. Python: ABC in dedicated module. Use: plugin systems, dependency injection, cross-boundary. Interface owned by client.
Design Patterns.hard: Separated Interface: define interface in separate package from implementation. Decouples client from implementation. Allows multiple implementations swapped at runtime. Python: ABC in dedicated module. Use: plugin systems, dependency injection, cross-boundary definitions. Interface owned by client.
Design Patterns.expert: Separated Interface: define interface in separate package from implementation. Decouples client from implementation. Allows multiple implementations swapped at runtime. Python: ABC in dedicated module. Use: plugin systems, dependency injection, cross-boundary definitions. Interface owned by client. Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Registry pattern (DDD).
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Registry.
Design Patterns.normal: Registry: global object for looking up. Service locator variation. Types: singleton registry global, thread-local registry. Replaces passing references throughout object graph. Use with caution: hidden dependencies. Prefer DI container over registry.
Design Patterns.hard: Registry: global object for looking up references to domain objects. Service locator variation. Types: singleton registry (global), thread-local registry (per-thread), request-scoped. Replaces passing references throughout object graph. Use with caution: hidden dependencies. Prefer DI container over registry.
Design Patterns.expert: Registry: global object for looking up references to domain objects. Service locator variation. Types: singleton registry (global), thread-local registry (per-thread), request-scoped. Replaces passing references throughout object graph. Use with caution: hidden dependencies. Prefer DI container over registry. Evaluate trade-offs before deciding.

Design Patterns.front: How does the Factory (DDD) pattern work?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Factory.
Design Patterns.normal: DDD Factory: encapsulates complex aggregate creation. Creates valid aggregate with all invariants. Separates creation from domain logic. Factory method on aggregate root. Separate Factory class for complex creation. Ensures aggregates are always in valid.
Design Patterns.hard: DDD Factory: encapsulates complex aggregate creation logic. Creates valid aggregate with all invariants satisfied. Separates creation from domain logic. Factory method on aggregate root for simple creation. Separate Factory class for complex creation. Ensures aggregates are always in valid state.
Design Patterns.expert: DDD Factory: encapsulates complex aggregate creation logic. Creates valid aggregate with all invariants satisfied. Separates creation from domain logic. Factory method on aggregate root for simple creation. Separate Factory class for complex creation. Ensures aggregates are always in valid state. Consider performance and maintainability.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Ports and Adapters (Hexagonal) architecture.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Ports.
Design Patterns.normal: Hexagonal architecture: application core domain isolated. Ports: interfaces defining how core communicates. Adapters: implementations of ports . Test: swap adapters . Main: Dependency Inversion Principle.
Design Patterns.hard: Hexagonal architecture: application core (domain) isolated from external systems. Ports: interfaces defining how core communicates externally (inbound/outbound). Adapters: implementations of ports (REST, DB, message queue, UI). Test: swap adapters (in-memory DB, test API). Main: Dependency Inversion Principle.
Design Patterns.expert: Hexagonal architecture: application core (domain) isolated from external systems. Ports: interfaces defining how core communicates externally (inbound/outbound). Adapters: implementations of ports (REST, DB, message queue, UI). Test: swap adapters (in-memory DB, test API). Main: Dependency Inversion Principle. Evaluate trade-offs before deciding.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Onion Architecture?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Onion.
Design Patterns.normal: Onion: concentric layers with dependencies inward. Core: domain model (entities, value objects). Application services: use cases. Infrastructure: persistence, external APIs Presentation: UI/API. Domain has no dependencies. Everything depends on domain. Dependency inversion: interfaces defined in inner.
Design Patterns.hard: Onion: concentric layers with dependencies inward. Core: domain model (entities, value objects). Application services: use cases. Infrastructure: persistence, external APIs. Presentation: UI/API. Domain has no dependencies. Everything depends on domain. Dependency inversion: interfaces defined in inner layers.
Design Patterns.expert: Onion: concentric layers with dependencies inward. Core: domain model (entities, value objects). Application services: use cases. Infrastructure: persistence, external APIs. Presentation: UI/API. Domain has no dependencies. Everything depends on domain. Dependency inversion: interfaces defined in inner layers. Evaluate trade-offs before deciding.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Clean Architecture.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Clean.
Design Patterns.normal: Clean Architecture Uncle Bob: entities. Dependency rule: dependencies point inward. Outer layers are details, swappable.
Design Patterns.hard: Clean Architecture (Uncle Bob): entities (enterprise business rules) -> use cases (application business rules) -> interface adapters (controllers, presenters, gateways) -> frameworks (web, DB, UI). Dependency rule: dependencies point inward. Outer layers (DB, framework) are details, swappable.
Design Patterns.expert: Clean Architecture (Uncle Bob): entities (enterprise business rules) -> use cases (application business rules) -> interface adapters (controllers, presenters, gateways) -> frameworks (web, DB, UI). Dependency rule: dependencies point inward. Outer layers (DB, framework) are details, swappable. Context determines the best approach.

Design Patterns.front: How does the Service Layer pattern work?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Service.
Design Patterns.normal: Service Layer: defines application boundary. Coordinates between domain objects, repositories, external. Implements transactions, authorization. Types: service interface + implementation. FastAPI routes call service methods.
Design Patterns.hard: Service Layer: defines application boundary with use cases. Coordinates between domain objects, repositories, external services. Implements transactions, authorization. Types: service interface + implementation, or thin service calling domain logic. FastAPI routes call service methods.
Design Patterns.expert: Service Layer: defines application boundary with use cases. Coordinates between domain objects, repositories, external services. Implements transactions, authorization. Types: service interface + implementation, or thin service calling domain logic. FastAPI routes call service methods. Evaluate trade-offs before deciding.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Data Mapper vs Active Record trade-offs.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Data.
Design Patterns.normal: Data Mapper: domain objects don't know. More testable , pure domain model. Active Record: domain objects handle own. Faster to implement Violates SRP. Data Mapper for complex domains. Active Record for simple CRUD apps.
Design Patterns.hard: Data Mapper: domain objects don't know DB. Repository maps. More testable (mock repository), pure domain model. More code. Active Record: domain objects handle own persistence (save, delete, find). Faster to implement. Violates SRP. Data Mapper for complex domains. Active Record for simple CRUD apps.
Design Patterns.expert: Data Mapper: domain objects don't know DB. Repository maps. More testable (mock repository), pure domain model. More code. Active Record: domain objects handle own persistence (save, delete, find). Faster to implement. Violates SRP. Data Mapper for complex domains. Active Record for simple CRUD apps. Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Table Module pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Table.
Design Patterns.normal: Table Module: single class handles business. Multiple instances vs single class. Used with Record Set . Less common in Python. SQLAlchemy: table reflection + dynamic classes. For table-oriented thinking rather than object-oriented.
Design Patterns.hard: Table Module: single class handles business logic for all rows in table. Multiple instances vs single class. Used with Record Set (DataSet in .NET). Less common in Python. SQLAlchemy: table reflection + dynamic classes. For table-oriented thinking rather than object-oriented.
Design Patterns.expert: Table Module: single class handles business logic for all rows in table. Multiple instances vs single class. Used with Record Set (DataSet in .NET). Less common in Python. SQLAlchemy: table reflection + dynamic classes. For table-oriented thinking rather than object-oriented. Context determines the best approach.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Transaction Script pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Transaction.
Design Patterns.normal: Transaction Script: organizes logic as single. Good for simple operations. Becomes unwieldy for complex logic (duplication). Use: simple CRUD, quick implementations. For complex problems: Domain Model pattern.
Design Patterns.hard: Transaction Script: organizes logic as single procedure per use case. Simple, procedural. Good for simple operations. Becomes unwieldy for complex logic (duplication). Use: simple CRUD, quick implementations. For complex problems: Domain Model pattern preferred.
Design Patterns.expert: Transaction Script: organizes logic as single procedure per use case. Simple, procedural. Good for simple operations. Becomes unwieldy for complex logic (duplication). Use: simple CRUD, quick implementations. For complex problems: Domain Model pattern preferred. Context determines the best approach.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Domain Model pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Domain.
Design Patterns.normal: Domain Model: rich object model. Combines data and behavior. Complex class relationships. Scalable to complex business logic. Requires ORM mapping (Data Mapper). High development effort upfront Enterprise applications. DDD promotes Domain Model pattern.
Design Patterns.hard: Domain Model: rich object model with business logic, invariants, rules. Combines data and behavior. Complex class relationships. Scalable to complex business logic. Requires ORM mapping (Data Mapper). High development effort upfront. Enterprise applications. DDD promotes Domain Model pattern.
Design Patterns.expert: Domain Model: rich object model with business logic, invariants, rules. Combines data and behavior. Complex class relationships. Scalable to complex business logic. Requires ORM mapping (Data Mapper). High development effort upfront. Enterprise applications. DDD promotes Domain Model pattern. Context determines the best approach.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Active Record pattern in Python.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Active.
Design Patterns.normal: Django ORM follows Active Record: model. Model.save(), Model.objects.get(), model.delete(). Business logic in model methods Simple. Violates SRP (persistence + domain). SQLAlchemy declarative similar to Active Record.
Design Patterns.hard: Django ORM follows Active Record: model class maps to table, instance maps to row.  Model.save(), Model.objects.get(), model.delete(). Business logic in model methods. Simple, intuitive. Violates SRP (persistence + domain). SQLAlchemy declarative similar to Active Record, but underlying Data Mapper.
Design Patterns.expert: Django ORM follows Active Record: model class maps to table, instance maps to row.  Model.save(), Model.objects.get(), model.delete(). Business logic in model methods. Simple, intuitive. Violates SRP (persistence + domain). SQLAlchemy declarative similar to Active Record, but underlying Data Mapper. Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Identity Map pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Identity.
Design Patterns.normal: Identity Map: ensures each object loaded. Maintains map of ID -> object. Subsequent loads return same instance . Prevents stale data, keeps consistent view. SQLAlchemy Identity Map in Session. Django QuerySet cache serves similar purpose.
Design Patterns.hard: Identity Map: ensures each object loaded only once per transaction. Maintains map of ID -> object. Subsequent loads return same instance (reference equality). Prevents stale data, keeps consistent view. SQLAlchemy Identity Map in Session. Django QuerySet cache serves similar purpose.
Design Patterns.expert: Identity Map: ensures each object loaded only once per transaction. Maintains map of ID -> object. Subsequent loads return same instance (reference equality). Prevents stale data, keeps consistent view. SQLAlchemy Identity Map in Session. Django QuerySet cache serves similar purpose. Consider performance and maintainability.

Design Patterns.front: How does the Query Object pattern work?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Query.
Design Patterns.normal: Query Object: represents DB query. Encapsulates filter criteria, sorting, pagination. Builder pattern for query construction. Python: SQLAlchemy Query object (session.query(...).filter(...).order_by(...)). Separates query construction from execution. Reusable query specifications.
Design Patterns.hard: Query Object: represents DB query as object. Encapsulates filter criteria, sorting, pagination. Builder pattern for query construction. Python: SQLAlchemy Query object (session.query(...).filter(...).order_by(...)). Separates query construction from execution. Reusable query specifications.
Design Patterns.expert: Query Object: represents DB query as object. Encapsulates filter criteria, sorting, pagination. Builder pattern for query construction. Python: SQLAlchemy Query object (session.query(...).filter(...).order_by(...)). Separates query construction from execution. Reusable query specifications. Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Metadata Mapping pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Metadata.
Design Patterns.normal: Metadata Mapping: defines mapping between objects. ORMs use metadata mapping for column. SQLAlchemy: declarative mapping (Column types, relationships). Hibernate: XML/annotation mapping.
Design Patterns.hard: Metadata Mapping: defines mapping between objects and DB tables in metadata (XML, annotations, dict). ORMs use metadata mapping for column mapping, relationship mapping, inheritance mapping. SQLAlchemy: declarative mapping (Column types, relationships). Hibernate: XML/annotation mapping.
Design Patterns.expert: Metadata Mapping: defines mapping between objects and DB tables in metadata (XML, annotations, dict). ORMs use metadata mapping for column mapping, relationship mapping, inheritance mapping. SQLAlchemy: declarative mapping (Column types, relationships). Hibernate: XML/annotation mapping. Consider performance and maintainability.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Lazy Load pattern in ORM?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Lazy.
Design Patterns.normal: Lazy Load: related objects loaded only. SQLAlchemy: lazy='select' separate query on access. N+1 problem: avoid lazy loading. Django: select_related , prefetch_related .
Design Patterns.hard: Lazy Load: related objects loaded only when accessed. SQLAlchemy: lazy='select' (separate query on access), lazy='joined' (JOIN in same query), lazy='subquery' (subquery). N+1 problem: avoid lazy loading in loops (use eager loading). Django: select_related (JOIN), prefetch_related (separate query + merge).
Design Patterns.expert: Lazy Load: related objects loaded only when accessed. SQLAlchemy: lazy='select' (separate query on access), lazy='joined' (JOIN in same query), lazy='subquery' (subquery). N+1 problem: avoid lazy loading in loops (use eager loading). Django: select_related (JOIN), prefetch_related (separate query + merge). Choose based on your specific requirements.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Identity Field pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Identity.
Design Patterns.normal: Identity Field: stores DB primary key. Pattern for mapping object identity. Strategies: assigned key, generated key . SQLAlchemy: Column(Integer, primary_key=True) Django: AutoField. Surrogate key vs natural key .
Design Patterns.hard: Identity Field: stores DB primary key in object. Pattern for mapping object identity to DB row. Strategies: assigned key, generated key (auto-increment, UUID, sequence). SQLAlchemy: Column(Integer, primary_key=True). Django: AutoField. Surrogate key (auto-increment) vs natural key (business meaning).
Design Patterns.expert: Identity Field: stores DB primary key in object. Pattern for mapping object identity to DB row. Strategies: assigned key, generated key (auto-increment, UUID, sequence). SQLAlchemy: Column(Integer, primary_key=True). Django: AutoField. Surrogate key (auto-increment) vs natural key (business meaning). Evaluate trade-offs before deciding.

Design Patterns.front: How does the Foreign Key Mapping pattern work?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Foreign.
Design Patterns.normal: Foreign Key Mapping: maps object association. Many-to-one: FK in child table. One-to-many: FK in child with backref. Many-to-many: junction table. SQLAlchemy: relationship('Other', foreign_keys=[...]). Django: ForeignKey, ManyToManyField. Direction of navigation affects mapping.
Design Patterns.hard: Foreign Key Mapping: maps object association to foreign key column. Many-to-one: FK in child table. One-to-many: FK in child with backref. Many-to-many: junction table. SQLAlchemy: relationship('Other', foreign_keys=[...]). Django: ForeignKey, ManyToManyField. Direction of navigation affects mapping.
Design Patterns.expert: Foreign Key Mapping: maps object association to foreign key column. Many-to-one: FK in child table. One-to-many: FK in child with backref. Many-to-many: junction table. SQLAlchemy: relationship('Other', foreign_keys=[...]). Django: ForeignKey, ManyToManyField. Direction of navigation affects mapping. Context determines the best approach.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Association Table Mapping pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Association.
Design Patterns.normal: Association Table: maps many-to-many relationship. Separate table with two FKs. SQLAlchemy: Table, Column. Django: ManyToManyField creates join table automatically. Additional columns on association table .
Design Patterns.hard: Association Table: maps many-to-many relationship via junction table. Separate table with two FKs. SQLAlchemy: Table('association', Base.metadata, Column('left_id', ...), Column('right_id', ...)). Django: ManyToManyField creates join table automatically. Additional columns on association table (order, quantity).
Design Patterns.expert: Association Table: maps many-to-many relationship via junction table. Separate table with two FKs. SQLAlchemy: Table('association', Base.metadata, Column('left_id', ...), Column('right_id', ...)). Django: ManyToManyField creates join table automatically. Additional columns on association table (order, quantity). Evaluate trade-offs before deciding.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Dependent Mapping pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Dependent.
Design Patterns.normal: Dependent Mapping: child object cannot exist. Cascade persistence: save parent cascades. SQLAlchemy: cascade='all, delete-orphan'. Delete-orphan: removes children no longer. No separate repository for dependent objects. Value objects mapped as dependent.
Design Patterns.hard: Dependent Mapping: child object cannot exist without parent. Cascade persistence: save parent cascades to children. SQLAlchemy: cascade='all, delete-orphan'. Delete-orphan: removes children no longer in collection. No separate repository for dependent objects. Value objects mapped as dependent.
Design Patterns.expert: Dependent Mapping: child object cannot exist without parent. Cascade persistence: save parent cascades to children. SQLAlchemy: cascade='all, delete-orphan'. Delete-orphan: removes children no longer in collection. No separate repository for dependent objects. Value objects mapped as dependent. Consider performance and maintainability.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Serialized LOB pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Serialized.
Design Patterns.normal: Serialized LOB: stores object graph. No join queries, simple schema. Cons: no queryability inside blob, coupling. Use: value objects, simple data structures. PostgreSQL JSONB for queryable JSON storage.
Design Patterns.hard: Serialized LOB: stores object graph as serialized blob (JSON, pickle, XML) in single column. No join queries, simple schema. Cons: no queryability inside blob, coupling to serialization. Use: value objects, simple data structures, configuration blobs. PostgreSQL JSONB for queryable JSON storage.
Design Patterns.expert: Serialized LOB: stores object graph as serialized blob (JSON, pickle, XML) in single column. No join queries, simple schema. Cons: no queryability inside blob, coupling to serialization. Use: value objects, simple data structures, configuration blobs. PostgreSQL JSONB for queryable JSON storage. Evaluate trade-offs before deciding.

Design Patterns.front: Explain the Concrete Table Inheritance pattern.
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Concrete.
Design Patterns.normal: Concrete Table Inheritance: each concrete class. No shared table. Polymorphic queries across classes impossible . SQLAlchemy: __tablename__ per class, no inheritance. Simpler, no nullable columns. Duplicate columns across tables.
Design Patterns.hard: Concrete Table Inheritance: each concrete class has its own table. No shared table. Polymorphic queries across classes impossible (UNION needed). SQLAlchemy: __tablename__ per class, no inheritance mapping. Simpler, no nullable columns. Duplicate columns across tables.
Design Patterns.expert: Concrete Table Inheritance: each concrete class has its own table. No shared table. Polymorphic queries across classes impossible (UNION needed). SQLAlchemy: __tablename__ per class, no inheritance mapping. Simpler, no nullable columns. Duplicate columns across tables. Context determines the best approach.

Design Patterns.front: What is the Single Table Inheritance pattern?
Design Patterns.easy: It helps you learn about Single.
